cards.title: Stop Guessing: A Visual Workspace to Debug Your AI Agents' Brains
cards.thesis: As builders push LLMs beyond simple chat, they're hitting major roadblocks managing complex multi-step AI agents and understanding *why* they do what they do. People are struggling with clunky terminal interfaces for multiple AI sessions and desperately want to see the AI's 'thought process' (its internal steps and reasoning) to verify its work and debug problems.

evidence.text: People are getting confused managing multiple Claude sessions from the terminal. There's no good way to keep track.
Dear Anthropic, can we please have thought traces back? I can't verify whether or not the LLM is arriving at the conclusion from cheating, or if it's fudging or making stuff up.
The ReAct pattern (where an AI thinks, acts, then thinks again) seems to work great, but people are asking how it's actually used in production systems. They need practical examples and tools.
For LLMs, what's a good format for structured or tabular data? What makes them grasp the data easily and efficiently?

cards.opportunity: Right now, building complex AI agents means wrestling with opaque outputs and confusing terminal sessions. There's a massive gap for a visual workspace that lets builders literally map out their agent's 'thought process' (how it plans and uses tools) and debug it step-by-step. Imagine a drag-and-drop builder for AI workflows that makes it easy to see where your agent gets stuck or 'hallucinates,' letting you connect different LLM calls and external tools with clear inputs and outputs.

cards.title: Your Search Engine is 'Enshitified': The Anti-AI, No-Bubble Search Opportunity
cards.thesis: Builders and researchers are getting increasingly frustrated with mainstream search engines (like Google and DuckDuckGo) because they're 'enshitifying' results by filtering, ignoring exact phrases, and pushing AI chatbot summaries. There's a clear demand for a search experience that prioritizes raw, multiple-source information, allowing users to cross-check facts themselves, especially as AI also fuels a surge in misinformation and scams.

evidence.text: One user stated, 'it now the turn of DuckDuckGo to enshitify my searches by bubblification and ignoring quotes,' indicating a strong frustration with current search engine behavior.
The same user explicitly said they are 'not interested in IA chatbot, I prefer multiple sources and to cross-check the information myself,' highlighting a desire for non-AI, verifiable information.

An Interpol report, with 439 engagements, notes that 'AI fuels more than half of cybercrime in Africa as scams surge,' which underscores the growing need for reliable, verifiable information sources to combat misinformation.

cards.opportunity: People are actively looking for alternatives because Google and DuckDuckGo are now 'bubblifying' and ignoring exact quotes, making it impossible to find precise info or escape algorithmic filters. Instead of another AI chatbot, ship a super-focused search aggregator that *guarantees* no AI summarization and no algorithmic bubble, just direct links to *multiple sources* (think documentation, specific forums, open-source repos). The first person to launch a tool that lets builders easily cross-check facts without an AI filter owns the 'I just want the damn truth' search market, and you could build a basic version this weekend by stitching together a few targeted scrapers.

cards.title: Your Next App is Private AF: AI Models Just Landed on Your Phone & Mac, No Cloud Needed
cards.thesis: Forget sending your data to the cloud for AI. Powerful AI models that used to need huge server farms can now run directly on your personal devices like iPhones and Macs, using very little memory and running super fast. This means you can build apps that are inherently private, work offline, and don't rack up expensive API bills, opening up a whole new design space for personal AI.

evidence.text: A new AI model (Maple-Preview, a type called Mixture of Experts) can run on an iPhone at a speed of 120 tokens per second, which is really fast for a mobile device.

Developers are showing off how to run very large AI models (like an 80-billion parameter Qwen model) on a Mac using only 4.3 GB of memory, and even a 35-billion parameter model on an iPhone. This means powerful AI is becoming accessible on everyday devices.
One project demonstrates a desktop wallpaper for Mac that animates like a vinyl record and syncs to Spotify, showing a general interest in personalized, local desktop utilities.

cards.opportunity: Most AI apps are still sending all your data to the cloud, but powerful models can now run right on your Mac or iPhone, fast and using minimal memory. This opens up a huge gap for hyper-private, offline-first tools. Imagine a smart desktop agent that summarizes your local documents, manages your personal knowledge base, or even helps you draft emails based on your private files – all without ever touching a server or costing you API fees. The first builder to truly nail a privacy-first local AI utility for everyday tasks owns this emerging market.

cards.title: Unleashing AI Artistry: The Hidden Goldmine in Simplifying Complex ComfyUI Workflows
cards.thesis: Builders are creating sophisticated 'director' tools for ComfyUI (a visual, node-based interface for AI image generation) that allow incredibly fine-tuned control over the AI's output. These tools, like the 'MiniMax H3 Director workflow,' break down complex image creation into multiple steps, giving artists and creators unprecedented power to guide the AI, but they're still too technical for most to use effectively out-of-the-box.

evidence.text: A GitHub project called 'ComfyUI MiniMax H3 Director workflow' has received 98 engagements, indicating strong interest in tools that guide complex AI image generation processes within ComfyUI.

Another project, 'Multi-segment MiniMax H3 Director for official ComfyUI MiniMax-H3,' garnered 75 engagements, showing that people are actively seeking and building tools for multi-step, detailed control over AI image generation.

cards.opportunity: Everyone's building these insane, multi-step ComfyUI workflows to get super specific AI art, but sharing and customizing them is still a huge pain because you have to dive deep into the node editor. What nobody's done is create a 'preset store' or a 'template configurator' for these advanced workflows, where a user can pick a 'MiniMax H3 Director' template, tweak a few simple sliders for their specific needs (like 'mood' or 'style'), and hit go without ever seeing a node. The first person to build a simple web UI that lets creators package and sell these complex ComfyUI workflows as one-click, customizable templates will own a massive chunk of the 'prosumer AI art' market.

cards.title: Don't Get Blocked: The Underground Market for Ultra-Fast Internet Access is Booming
cards.thesis: People in regions with internet restrictions are constantly searching for reliable 'airport' services (specialized proxies or VPNs) to access the global internet. The demand for the 'latest' and 'high-performance' solutions, along with easy setup guides for tools like Clash or V2Ray (popular software for routing internet traffic through these services), is huge and always changing.

evidence.text: People are actively looking for the 'latest high-performance airport recommendations' for 'scientific internet access' (bypassing censorship) and need 'detailed configuration tutorials' for tools like Clash and V2Ray.
The repeated emphasis on '2026 latest' and 'recommendations' across multiple repos highlights a constant, urgent need for up-to-date, reliable services and clear setup guides.

cards.opportunity: Everyone's scrambling for the 'latest high-performance airport recommendations' because what works today might be blocked tomorrow. Instead of static GitHub lists, a dynamic platform that tracks, reviews, and simplifies setup for these services (like VPNs for specific regions) would be massive. You could build a site that aggregates user reviews, offers one-click config downloads for popular clients like Clash, and even provides real-time speed tests, making it the go-to trusted source for bypassing internet restrictions.

cards.title: YC S23 Companies Are Staffing Up: Your Chance to Spot Early Trends
cards.thesis: Recently funded Y Combinator S23 companies like Truemetrics and Roame are quickly moving to build out their core leadership teams, focusing on critical functions like Go-To-Market (sales/marketing) and engineering. This indicates they're transitioning from initial product development to scaling their market reach and technical foundations, prioritizing these roles early on.

evidence.text: Truemetrics (YC S23) is hiring a GTM Lead in Berlin, showing an early focus on market entry and sales strategy.
Roame (YC S23) is hiring a Lead Engineer, highlighting the need for strong technical leadership right after their accelerator batch.

cards.opportunity: Early-stage YC companies like Truemetrics and Roame are prioritizing senior Go-To-Market (sales/marketing) and engineering talent from the get-go. Instead of competing on general job boards, you could create a highly curated talent network or a specialized recruiting tool specifically for YC S23 (and future cohorts) focusing on these critical, early-stage leadership roles, positioning yourself as the go-to resource for fast-growing startups needing to staff up quickly post-accelerator.
